why: Different kinds of businesses get targeted in different ways. Freight brokers see far more payment fraud; cold storage sites rely more on connected equipment.
More people means more logins to manage, and more chances for a shared or forgotten account.

text: Who looks after your computers and IT?
why: An outside IT company usually has admin access to everything, so a breach at their end reaches you too. If nobody is in charge, updates get missed and recovering from an attack takes much longer.

text: If your computers stopped working, how long before you start losing serious money?
why: This tells us how badly an outage like ransomware would hurt. The faster the losses start, the higher the impact.

text: Do you handle perishable goods (food, livestock, or temperature-sensitive cargo)?
why: When goods can spoil, even a short disruption turns into real losses for you and your customers.

text: Do your top 3 customers make up more than half your revenue?
why: If a few big customers matter most, an incident that affects them, or a failed security audit, could hit you hard.

text: Do you send or receive bank transfers to suppliers, carriers, or growers every week?
why: Regular transfers are exactly what payment fraud criminals look for. They try to slip their own bank details into a routine payment.

text: Do you store employee SINs, banking details, or customer payment info?
why: Losing or leaking this kind of information can bring legal duties, notification costs, and lost trust.
A website that takes orders or logins has to be built and kept up securely. If you have no website, we mark that part of the standards as not applicable instead of leaving a gap.

options.label: Yes, with online ordering, payments, or customer logins

text: Do you have equipment connected to the internet, like refrigeration monitoring, grain systems, sensors, or cameras?
why: Connected equipment can be reached from outside. If you are not sure, we will assume yes so we do not miss a risk.

text: Do people use phones or tablets for work email, dispatch, or apps?
why: Phones carry email, load details, and saved passwords. Company-owned devices can be locked down centrally; personal phones need work data kept separate so it can be removed if one is lost or someone leaves.

text: What do you use for email?
why: We use this to give you step-by-step instructions for the system you actually have. The domain check on the next screen can fill this in for you.
